tb21_profile.skill: Download a pretrained transformer to a local path, run tokenizer+model inference correctly, and wrap it in an HTTP endpoint that honours an exact JSON request/response contract including a 400 error path
tb21_profile.domain: Python ML serving stack — HuggingFace transformers/torch, Flask/WSGI, REST/JSON, background process management on a fixed host:port
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec plus configure-a-service: build a model-backed API to a written schema and leave it running in the background

searches: tools.py words tmax Flask "port 5000" "0.0.0.0" "in the background" POST model inference 400 -n 25
tools.py search tw "http server (on|listening)|expose an endpoint|POST request.*JSON|run .* in the background" -n 15
tools.py search rts "inference server|serve the model|model server|predictions? endpoint" -n 12

notes: TMax dominates: it has a whole family of 'train/load a model, serve it over Flask or FastAPI on a fixed port with an exact JSON schema, leave it running' tasks, several using HuggingFace models directly, so eight of the ten best overall are TMax. TerminalWorld is the weakest pool here — it has ML tasks and HTTP tasks but almost nothing that combines them, so its ranks 7-10 are filler. Note two retrieval traps: 'model' matches Django/SQLAlchemy ORM models all over SWE-Smith, and 'inference' matches Java 'var' type-inference tasks (a ~20-item near-duplicate family) and gg build-graph inference in RTS; I discarded both. No task anywhere in the pool uses huggingface_hub/from_pretrained by name, so the literal 'download and cache a model from the Hub' step has no exact precedent; tw_707448 (download a real .pth rather than an HTML page) is the nearest analogue.
